sources.title: Software Engineering at Google: Chapter 15, Deprecation
sources.read_scope: Complete chapter previously read and recorded in books-quality.json; complete main chapter reread for this package. Linked chapters and cited tooling were not reread.
sources.hash_limit: Hash identifies the prior research snapshot, not a newly downloaded copy or current live page.
sources.trigger: A supported technical contract is being retired.
sources.failure: Existing consumers remain or new ones appear while the migration stalls.
sources.mechanism: Discover use, assign responsibility, migrate, prevent fresh dependencies, and measure intermediate progress.
sources.limits: Technical systems with consumer visibility; not a public-product shutdown policy or a mandate for Google-specific tools, staffing, or outages.
sources.counterexample: Age alone does not make a working system obsolete.
sources.verification: Proposed per-consumer compatibility and removal checks; no live retirement or effectiveness experiment performed.

sources.title: PEP 387: Backwards Compatibility Policy
sources.author: Benjamin Peterson
sources.read_scope: Public API scope, Basic policy for backwards compatibility, Soft Deprecation, Making Incompatible Changes, and changelog; not linked discussion threads.
sources.trigger: A policy label is being treated as a removal schedule.
sources.failure: Soft deprecation is mistaken for permission to remove supported behavior.
sources.mechanism: Record the actual policy state and apply its transition requirements.
sources.limits: This policy governs Python's language and standard library; its grace periods and governance do not govern arbitrary projects.
sources.counterexample: A supported soft-deprecated interface can remain available without a scheduled removal.
sources.verification: Inspect the target's actual support policy; proposed test retains a supported legacy consumer.

sources.title: Python warnings: Warning control
sources.read_scope: Warning Categories, Warnings Filter/default filters, Testing Warnings, Updating Code For New Versions of Dependencies, and deprecated decorator documentation. No runtime execution.
sources.trigger: A warning or deprecation annotation is offered as proof that new use is blocked.
sources.failure: Runtime filters hide warnings or diagnostic output does not fail the selected build.
sources.mechanism: Inspect installed tooling and verify visibility plus actual enforcement under the configured check.
sources.limits: Decorator availability is runtime-version-dependent; runtime category does not determine static checker diagnostics. Documentation alone cannot establish a project's CI behavior.
sources.counterexample: An ignored DeprecationWarning can coexist with successful continued use.
sources.verification: Proposed allowed-existing and forbidden-new-use controls; no Python warning probe executed in this task.

repository_applications.trigger: A caller search or quiet usage interval is presented as complete discovery.
repository_applications.failure: Infrequent, dynamic, external, or retained-input consumers are omitted.
repository_applications.mechanism: Record evidence coverage by source, environment, version, path, and observation interval; preserve unknowns.
repository_applications.limits: A finite observed domain supports conclusions only about that domain.
repository_applications.counterexample: A monthly job can be absent from a shorter usage report.
repository_applications.verification: Independent fixture exposes a periodic or indirect consumer and requires a justified next gate.

repository_applications.trigger: A replacement exists but retirement parity is uncertain.
repository_applications.failure: Provider-level success conceals a changed consumer error, side effect, or data format.
repository_applications.mechanism: Classify required behavior as preserved, intentionally changed, or unresolved and verify representative consumers.
repository_applications.limits: Authorized withdrawal can replace parity; unresolved behavior cannot silently become an approved change.
repository_applications.counterexample: A new method with the same parameter names can persist an incompatible format.
repository_applications.verification: Independent staged-migration fixture tests a consumer-specific semantic or recovery boundary.

repository_applications.trigger: Migration progress is undermined by newly introduced use.
repository_applications.failure: A warning appears but the intended dependency rule is not enforced.
repository_applications.mechanism: Choose the precise adoption boundary and test permitted legacy use alongside a prohibited new dependency.
repository_applications.limits: A project-level dependency rule does not necessarily block additional calls inside an existing consumer; state actual scope.
repository_applications.counterexample: A rule that rejects every existing consumer can break the promised staged transition.
repository_applications.verification: Separate allowed and forbidden controls against the real configured guard.
